title: Static Initialization
summary: Master static blocks ('static { ... }'): one-time execution during class loading to initialize complex class-level data.
learningOutcomes: Write and trace static initialization blocks
Understand the exact sequence: Static blocks execute once on class load, BEFORE any constructor
Initialize complex static collections and configurations safely

activities.title: Everyday Analogy: Setting Up the Electric Grid Before Opening Factory Doors

analogy.story:
Imagine a high-tech car manufacturing facility.

Before the very first worker walks through the door, and before the very first automobile chassis is assembled on the conveyor belt, the building's Master Power Plant must be fired up. High-voltage transformers are calibrated, water pumps are pressurized, and network servers are booted. This complex infrastructure setup happens exactly ONCE when the factory opens.

After that, every time a new car is assembled, only the normal car assembly process runs (Constructor).

A static initialization block is that factory power plant startup: it executes one-time setup logic when the class is first loaded, long before any constructor runs.
analogy.takeaway: Static blocks execute once upon class loading to prepare complex class-level resources. Constructors execute repeatedly for every individual object born.

activities.title: The Static Initialization Block Syntax & Order of Execution

rules: Rule 1: Static blocks run before any constructor runs.
Rule 2: If a class has multiple static blocks, they run in top-down appearance order.
Rule 3: Static blocks cannot throw checked exceptions without catching them inside the block.

keyTakeaways: Rule 1: Static blocks run before any constructor runs.
Rule 2: If a class has multiple static blocks, they run in top-down appearance order.
Rule 3: Static blocks cannot throw checked exceptions without catching them inside the block.

questions.prompt: When does a static initialization block execute in Java?
questions.question: When does a static initialization block execute in Java?
options: Every time an object is instantiated with 'new'
Exactly once, when the class is first loaded into memory by the JVM
When the operating system boots
Whenever a garbage collection cycle finishes
questions.explanation: Static blocks execute exactly once when the class is loaded by the ClassLoader.

questions.prompt: What is the relative execution order between a static block and a constructor?
questions.question: What is the relative execution order between a static block and a constructor?
options: The constructor runs first, then the static block
The static block always runs first, before any constructor executes
They execute concurrently in separate threads
The static block runs only after all objects are deleted
questions.explanation: Static blocks run at class-load time; constructors run subsequently when instances are created.

questions.prompt: If a class has two static initialization blocks, in what order do they run?
questions.question: If a class has two static initialization blocks, in what order do they run?
options: Random order determined by the JVM
In the exact order they appear in the source code file from top to bottom
The shorter block runs first
Only the second block runs; the first is ignored
questions.explanation: Java executes multiple static blocks sequentially from top to bottom as they appear in the file.

questions.prompt: Why would an engineer use a static block instead of a simple inline assignment (static int x = 10;)?
questions.question: Why would an engineer use a static block instead of a simple inline assignment (static int x = 10;)?
options: When initialization requires loops, multi-step logic, or exception handling (try-catch)
Because inline assignments are not supported in Java
To make variables private
To reduce bytecode file size
questions.explanation: Static blocks are ideal for multi-line logic, populating arrays/tables, or handling checked exceptions.

questions.prompt: Can a static block access instance variables directly?
questions.question: Can a static block access instance variables directly?
options: Yes, static blocks can access all variables
No, static blocks run before any instance exists and cannot touch non-static members
Only if the instance variables are declared public
Only if the class is an inner class
questions.explanation: No instance exists when a static block executes, so non-static members cannot be accessed.

questions.prompt: If a class is loaded and 100 objects of that class are created, how many times does the static block execute?
questions.question: If a class is loaded and 100 objects of that class are created, how many times does the static block execute?
options: 100 times
1 time
0 times
2 times
questions.explanation: Static initialization blocks run strictly once per class loading, regardless of the number of instances created.

questions.prompt: In our factory analogy, what does the Master Power Plant startup represent?
questions.question: In our factory analogy, what does the Master Power Plant startup represent?
options: The constructor
The static initialization block
The garbage collector
The compiler
questions.explanation: Powering up the factory once before building any car represents one-time static initialization.

questions.prompt: What happens if a static initialization block throws an uncaught runtime exception?
questions.question: What happens if a static initialization block throws an uncaught runtime exception?
options: The JVM ignores it and proceeds normally
The JVM throws ExceptionInInitializerError and the class fails to load, preventing any object creation
The static block re-runs automatically
The class becomes abstract
questions.explanation: An unhandled exception in a static block causes an ExceptionInInitializerError, making the class unusable.

questions.prompt: Can you declare a return type for a static initialization block?
questions.question: Can you declare a return type for a static initialization block?
options: Yes, it must return void
No, static blocks have no method signature, no return type, and no parameters
Yes, it can return int
Only boolean
questions.explanation: Static blocks consist simply of 'static { ... }' with no parameters or return types.

questions.prompt: Can a class have both static blocks and instance initialization blocks?
questions.question: Can a class have both static blocks and instance initialization blocks?
options: No, Java permits only one or the other
Yes, static blocks run once on class load, while instance blocks run on every 'new' before the constructor body
Only in Java 8 and earlier
Only if the class is final
questions.explanation: Java supports both: static blocks for one-time class setup, and instance blocks for per-object setup.

questions.question: What is the exact sequence of initialization when a class is instantiated for the first time?
questions.answer: 1. Class is loaded: Static variables and static initialization blocks execute in top-down order. 2. Memory allocated on heap for new instance. 3. Instance variables initialized to default values, then explicit initializers and instance initializer blocks run. 4. Constructor body executes.
keyTakeaways: Static members (once) -> Instance fields/blocks -> Constructor body

questions.question: What causes an 'ExceptionInInitializerError' in Java?
questions.answer: An ExceptionInInitializerError is thrown when an unchecked exception (like NullPointerException, ArithmeticException, or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) is thrown inside a static initialization block or during static variable initialization and is not caught.

questions.question: Can a static block throw a checked exception (like IOException)?
questions.answer: A static block cannot throw a checked exception to the outside world because there is no caller to declare a 'throws' clause. Any checked exception occurring inside a static block must be caught with a try-catch block inside the static block itself.
keyTakeaways: No 'throws' clause allowed on static blocks

questions.question: What is an instance initialization block, and how does it differ from a static block?
questions.answer: An instance initialization block is written as '{ ... }' without the static keyword. It executes every time a new object is instantiated with 'new', right before the constructor body runs. A static block ('static { ... }') executes only once when the class is loaded.
keyTakeaways: Static block = runs once on class load

questions.question: Is it possible to execute code in Java without a main() method using static blocks?
questions.answer: In ancient Java versions (Java 6 and earlier), a static block could print and call System.exit(0) before the main check. However, in modern Java (Java 7+), the JVM strictly verifies the presence of a valid public static void main(String[] args) method before launching the class.
keyTakeaways: Modern JVM enforces main() check prior to launch

questions.question: Why should heavy operations (like network calls or large file I/O) be avoided in static initialization blocks?
questions.answer: Because class loading is synchronous and holds internal JVM class-loading locks. If a static block hangs or times out during a network call, the application thread freezes, potentially causing deadlocks or failing application bootstrap.

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Precomputed Factorial Table
practiceProblems.description: Write a complete FactorialLookup class from scratch with private static int[] factorials = new int[6]. In a static block, compute factorials for 0 through 5 (0! = 1, 1! = 1, 2! = 2, 3! = 6, 4! = 24, 5! = 120). Provide static getFactorial(int n) returning factorials[n] or -1 if out of range. In Main, print '5! = 120'.
